reduction.witness: The write-up does not prove the required statement g(t) >= 0 for every t. It would need to establish for arbitrary t that f^n(t)=t+n g(t)>0 for every n, forcing g(t)>=0; equation (4) is not iterated for arbitrary t in the text.
reduction.load_bearing: This sign conclusion is needed before the value set V can be restricted to zero and a possible positive constant. Without it, the written argument has not excluded negative values of g.

upper_bound.quote:
Thus $V$ contains **at most one** positive number.  Consequently, either  

* (i) $g\equiv 0$ (constant), which gives $f(x)=x$, a solution; or  
* (ii) there is $c>0$ such that $V \subseteq \{0, c\}$ with both values attainable.
upper_bound.witness: Counterexample to this dichotomy: take f(x)=x+1, so g(x)=1 and V={1}. This function satisfies the original inequalities by QM-AM-GM, and V has at most one positive value, but g is not identically zero and the second branch fails because both 0 and 1 are not attainable. Negative values of g also have not yet been excluded in the text.
upper_bound.load_bearing: This is the case split on which the remainder of the necessity proof is based. The subsequent argument only treats the mixed case and therefore does not make the stated all-cases deduction valid.

parsed.notes: The functional equation and final verification are correct. However, orbit positivity is not proved, and the necessity argument relies on a false case split that omits the constant positive case.
